transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Verdant - Head of ML), Sofia Grant (Verdant - Eng Manager), Noah Patel (Verdant - Security Ops)

Summary: quick renewal and expansion check-in. Verdant wants to add EU (private) and bump reserved capacity by ~40% over next quarter. Security questions around KMS and SOC2. Agree to run throughput test and exchange pricing + SOW.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'll kick off, we're here to walk through the renewal and the growth ask you shared, add the eu region, and talk timeline. priya's with me for the technical bits.
[00:22] Liam: thanks alex. uh, so main thing for us is we want lower 95th p50 latency in eu, and also we need the data residency there. To private/VPC is preferred, but cost is a factor.
[00:35] Priya: yeah, understood. couple clarifying q's — when you say private, do you mean private control plane + customer-managed VPC or fully on-prem?
[00:45] Sofia: customer-managed VPC is our preference; full on-prem is possible but adds ops overhead. we want KMS integration to keep keys in our cloud account.
[00:56] Noah: and from security we'll want SOC2/iso artifacts early, and the ability to see audit logs — is that already in the private offering?
[01:08] Alex: short answer: yes. Redwood Private supports customer VPC plus KMS integration. we have audit logs and extended retention as an add-on. i'll send the security pack after this call.
[01:20] Liam: great. on capacity — our current contract renews in may, we're looking at a ~40% uplift to reserved capacity, but want staged commit: start with a 20% immediate top-up and then trigger another 20% in q3 if throughput validates.
[01:34] Priya: that's a sensible approach. from a runtime perspective we can suggest dedicated pools sized for your peak sequence lengths, and configure auto-burst for infrequent spikes to reduce steady-state cost.
[01:48] Sofia: can you give an idea of the latency tradeoff if we enable more batching + prefix cache? sometimes our prod flows are latency-sensitive.
[01:58] Priya: batching helps cost but can add ms to tail latency. We can tune per-route: low-latency routes get smaller batches + reserved capacity; high-throughput routes use larger batches. Also prefix/KV cache reduces token compute but needs warm-up.
[02:15] Liam: right. our chat frontend is sensitive; 95th latency target is 350ms for UI interactions — is that doable from eu region?
[02:24] Priya: 350ms 95th is tight but feasible with reserved capacity in eu central + local KV caching. We'll need your QPS numbers and typical sequence lengths to model it.
[02:36] Alex: action — liam, can you share QPS by route and average seq len? that helps us size the reserved pool and give you a realistic quote.
[02:45] Liam: yes, i'll send that.
[02:47] 
[05:00] (later in call)
[05:05] Noah: on KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or do you do envelope encryption? we want keys never stored by vendor.
[05:15] Priya: we support envelope encryption with customer KMS, keys never leave your account. For Private we can also integrate with HSMs if that's a blocker. sometimes the docs mix terms, i think you saw "Redwood Delicated" in a slide — that's just a typo — it's Redwood Dedicated/Dedicated pools.
[05:34] Noah: OK. and how granular are the audit logs? we need per-request metadata, timestamps, model version, and caller id.
[05:44] Alex: logs include request/response metadata, model id, timestamp; payloads are redacted by default but can be captured with consent. retention and export options are in the security pack i'll send.
[05:56] 
[10:12] Sofia: one concern — our infra team is worried about fallback behavior if the eu cluster hits capacity. does Redwood auto-failover to another region or a cheaper model variant?
[10:25] Priya: policy-based routing can fail over to a compatible model in another region or a lower-cost quantized variant. we'll default to canary fallback rules per route. you can also set hard SLOs to block cross-region fallback for sensitive routes.
[10:40] Liam: good. we want to avoid cross-border fallbacks for PII flows.
[10:45] Priya: noted — that's configurable.
[12:00] Alex: price question — if we do staged commitment (20% now, 20% later) can we get blended pricing?
[12:12] Alex: (continuing) typically we can do a tiered commitment with an initial discount for immediate commit and a hold-back clause to expand at a published uplift. i'll draft numbers.
[12:22] Liam: the budge... budgeting team asks for a cap on the monthly spend — can Redwood provide alerts + cost breakdown by token per route?
[12:33] Alex: yes, console provides token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards. we can set billing alerts and hard caps in contract.
[12:42] 
[18:05] (mid call, brief noise and overlap)
[18:10] Sofia: sorry, dog interrupted the meeting — but back. on the throughput test: what do you need from us to run the two-hour run?
[18:20] Priya: for the in-environment test we need a sample prompt set (you can redact PHI), expected QPS curve (5 minute granularity), auth creds for the test runner (we'll use temp keys), and a proposed window. We'll monitor latency, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.
[18:37] Liam: we'll provide that. can we also include a few long-form prompts to test memory/kv caching behaviors?
[18:44] Priya: absolutely — those are helpful to size KV memory and estimate tail behavior.
[21:00] Noah: any blockers on SOC2 evidence? we need to present to compliance for greenlight — is there an audit letter or sysdescr we can get?
[21:12] Alex: we have SOC2 Type II report and sysdescr packages for Private customers. i'll attach the redacted report and the SOC point-by-point mapping to your control matrix.
[21:25] Noah: great. also curious about pen test cadence — do you do annual pen tests and share the results?
[21:34] Alex: yes, annual pen test. for Private deployments we can share a summarized findings report.
[24:10] 
[28:05] Priya: technical note — if you plan to use long context windows we should discuss quantization profiles and kernel/compilation selection. for example, 32k tokens changes our batch sizing heuristics and may change GPU selection (A800 vs A100 equivalent).
[28:22] Sofia: good point — we currently have a couple of back-office LLMs using 16k and a couple of customer facing with 4k. most interactive routes are 1-2k.
[28:33] Priya: that distribution helps; we'll size mixed clusters to balance cost/latency.
[30:00] Alex: ok quick recap and commitments: alex to send pricing + blended staged commitment options; priya to share VPC/on-prem checklist and KMS integration notes; verdant to send QPS and sample prompts; schedule throughput test (propose 2026-03-24).
[30:18] Liam: yep that's fine. any legal paperwork to start now?
[30:25] Alex: we can issue a non-binding SOW draft and a quote; legal can run parallel once cost and scope are acceptable.
[30:38] Noah: final question: latency SLOs in contract — can you guarantee 95th <350ms for the chat route?
[30:46] Priya: we can contract SLOs for 95th at region-level with credits for breaches, but it depends on reserved sizing and network egress. we'll model it and propose a target with associated credits.
[30:59] 
[37:50] (wrap)
[37:55] Alex: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with a security pack and the pricing proposal by end of week. Priya will send the checklist. we'll reconvene after the throughput test results.
[38:08] Liam: thanks all. appreciate the quick turn.
[38:12] Sofia: thanks.
[38:14] Noah: thanks.

Notes: minor transcription errors present (e.g. 'Redwood Delicated' instead of Dedicated, 'KV cash' sometimes transcribed), speakers occasionally overlap.

End of transcript.
